items.content_html:
Summary

api.PushSubscription.subscriptionId claims Chrome support from 42 with no removal, so through the mirrors it also shows as supported in current Chrome Android, Opera, Opera Android and Samsung Internet. Chrome removed the attribute in Chrome 45 (2015), and Chromium-based Edge never had it. Once the Chrome removal is recorded ("version_removed": "45", plus "version_removed": "79" for Edge), npm run lint reports:

Obsolete - 4 problems (1 error, 0 warnings, 3 infos):
  ✖ api.PushSubscription.subscriptionId - Error → feature was implemented and has since been removed from all browsers dating back two or more years ago.

Firefox, Safari and WebView never supported it. Under the removal of irrelevant features guideline, this PR removes the feature instead of recording the removal.

Test results and supporting details

  • Chromium commit 64e7ce39c2fd (CL 1148763005, Blink r196315, landed 2015-06-02), "Remove support for PushSubscription.subscriptionId.", deletes [DeprecateAs=PushSubscriptionId] readonly attribute DOMString subscriptionId; from PushSubscription.idl. Its description says: "The subscriptionId property has been included in endpoint for Chrome 44, and is to be removed in Chrome 45".
  • Release mapping. Here is PushSubscription.idl at the Blink revision each release's DEPS pins:
    • 44.0.2403.157 (last Chrome 44 stable) still has the subscriptionId attribute.
    • 45.0.2454.0 (the M45 branch) does not.
  • The blink-dev Intent to Remove: PushSubscription.subscriptionId and "gcm_user_visible_only" in the Manifest (approved with three LGTMs, May 2015) says: "In Chrome 44, implementations should only be using the endpoint, but the subscriptionId was still exposed." and "In Chrome 45, we intent to only support the endpoint and PushSubscriptionOptions dictionary."
  • I checked Chromium 156 and Firefox 157. In both, 'subscriptionId' in PushSubscription.prototype is false. Object.getOwnPropertyNames(PushSubscription.prototype) is endpoint,expirationTime,options,getKey,toJSON,unsubscribe,constructor in Chromium.
  • Edge: Edge 79 is based on Chromium 79, long after the removal. I did not verify the existing Edge 17 data (it was a guess in #20238). Edge 18 was the last EdgeHTML release, so either way no current browser has had the feature for years.
  • npm test passes (format, lint, unit tests). The lint output keeps only the 3 obsolete infos that were already there.

Related issues

None. The MDN page PushSubscription: subscriptionId property (browser-compat: api.PushSubscription.subscriptionId) needs removing from mdn/content too.
items.title: Remove irrelevant `api.PushSubscription.subscriptionId`

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds api.MouseEvent.webkitForce, the non-standard Force Touch property. Safari 9, false everywhere else, and not standard track. The shape follows the existing Element webkitmouseforce* events.

The two constants named in the issue, WEBKIT_FORCE_AT_MOUSE_DOWN and WEBKIT_FORCE_AT_FORCE_MOUSE_DOWN, are left out because the API guidelines say not to add data for constants.

Safari on iOS mirrors Safari (so iOS 9). That differs from the force events, which are false on iOS because they never fire there. The property itself is on MouseEvent in every WebKit port. See the sources below.

Test results and supporting details

Following the research in the issue:

  • WebKit 5b920c8 (May 2015, bug 145065) renamed MouseEvent.force to webkitForce and added the two constants. That commit is WebKit 601.1.33. Safari 8 is 538.35 and Safari 9 is 601.1.56 in browsers/safari.json.
  • At the Safari 9 release tag, the attribute is in MouseEvent.idl behind Conditional=MOUSE_FORCE_EVENTS. FeatureDefines.h turns ENABLE_MOUSE_FORCE_EVENTS on by default for every port, with no iOS override and nothing in FeatureDefines.xcconfig.
  • Today the attribute has no condition at all (MouseEvent.idl at cc99e26).
  • Safari 26.4 on macOS 26.4.1: 'webkitForce' in MouseEvent.prototype is true, and new MouseEvent('click').webkitForce is 0.

I couldn't test Safari on iOS, so the iOS version comes from the build flags above.

Checks:

  • npm run lint -- api/MouseEvent.json: all data passed linting.
  • npm test: 349 tests pass, 0 lint errors.
  • npm run build: Safari, Safari on iOS and WebView on iOS all resolve to "9".

Related issues

Fixes #27334
items.title: Add MouseEvent.webkitForce

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds the note Requires macOS 26 or later. to Safari for css.properties.dynamic-range-limit and its standard and no-limit values. These are the three entries with Safari support. constrained and dynamic-range-limit-mix() are false in Safari and stay as they are.

As agreed in the issue, this is a note without partial_implementation. The behaviour depends on the OS having HDR support, which is the exception in the "Operating system limitations" guideline.

Safari on iOS gets its own {"version_added": "26"} statement instead of mirror. Otherwise the build would copy the macOS note to iOS. I didn't add an iOS note, because Safari 26 on iOS only ships with iOS 26, so the note would add nothing. WebView on iOS still mirrors Safari on iOS. If you would rather have Requires iOS 26 or later. on iOS too, like font-variation-settings has for iOS 11, I can add it.

Test results and supporting details

WebKit only exposes the property when the HDR display setting is on:

  • dynamic-range-limit has "settings-flag": "supportHDRDisplayEnabled" in CSSProperties.json.
  • SupportHDRDisplayEnabled defaults to ENABLE(SUPPORT_HDR_DISPLAY_BY_DEFAULT) in UnifiedWebPreferences.yaml.
  • ENABLE_SUPPORT_HDR_DISPLAY_BY_DEFAULT is set for PLATFORM(MAC) && __MAC_OS_X_VERSION_MIN_REQUIRED >= 260000, and for all of iOS and visionOS, in PlatformEnableCocoa.h.

This matches what the reporter found in the issue: CSS.supports("dynamic-range-limit: standard") is false in Safari 26 on macOS 15.

Checks:

  • npm run lint -- css/properties/dynamic-range-limit.json: all data passed linting.
  • npm test: 349 tests pass, 0 lint errors.
  • npm run build: Safari has the note, and Safari on iOS and WebView on iOS resolve to {"version_added": "26"} with no note.

Related issues

Fixes #29077
items.title: Add macOS 26 note to dynamic-range-limit in Safari

items.content_html:
Firefox supports style in Integrity-Policy blocked-destinations behind the security.integrity_policy.stylesheet.enabled pref in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1974247. Since the integrity-violation report type shipped in Firefox 149, these violations are reported with "style" as the body.destination.

This adds api.ReportingObserver.ReportingObserver.options_parameter.types_property.integrity-violation.destination_style, with Firefox 149 behind the pref, so the IntegrityViolationReport page can list "style" as a destination and show that no browser supports it by default.

Claude states this, but I have not verified it:

  • Firefox: dom/security/IntegrityPolicyService.cpp maps DestinationType::Style to "style" in the report body, and dom/security/IntegrityPolicy.cpp only adds Style when the pref is set. The pref is still false in main.
  • Chrome: false. services/network/public/cpp/integrity_policy_parser.cc only accepts script.
  • Safari: false. WebKit's Source/WebCore/loader/IntegrityPolicy.cpp hard-codes "script" as the report destination.

Related docs work can be tracked in mdn/content#46592
items.title: integrity-violation report: style destination behind Firefox pref

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds blob_url, data_url and srcdoc subfeatures to html.elements.iframe.loading, as proposed in #30950. The spec runs the lazy loading steps for srcdoc and for every URL scheme, but Chromium only lazy-loads http(s) URLs, and WebKit doesn't lazy-load blob: URLs.

The names follow webdriver.bidi.network.getData.data_url. I left the new keys untagged, so the loading-lazy web feature keeps its Baseline status until the web-features maintainers decide how to map them.

Test results and supporting details

npm test passes.

Manual test: a page with four loading="lazy" iframes 30,000 px below the viewport (same-origin http, srcdoc, data: and blob:). It records which iframes load before the window load event and which still haven't loaded 3 seconds later.

http(s) srcdoc data: blob:
Chrome 157 lazy loads at once loads at once loads at once
Safari 26.4 lazy lazy lazy loads at once

Firefox isn't installed here, so its data comes from the sources below.

Sources:

  • Chromium, false: IsFrameLazyLoadable() returns false for anything but http(s) URLs (html_frame_owner_element.cc). The open bug (crbug.com/40703417) only names srcdoc, so impl_url is only on that row.
  • Firefox 121: iframe lazy loading shipped in 121, when dom.iframe_lazy_loading.enabled became true by default (StaticPrefList.yaml at FIREFOX_121_0_RELEASE, nightly only in 120). Firefox's WPT expectations at that tag have no iframe-loading-lazy.html.ini (meta directory), so all five subtests, including the srcdoc, data: and blob: ones, were expected to pass. Those subtests have been in WPT since July 2020 (web-platform-tests/wpt@37281cb).
  • Safari 16.4 for srcdoc and data:, false for blob:: WebKit stopped restricting iframe lazy loading to http(s) URLs in July 2022 (252852@main, bug 243225), before iframe lazy loading shipped in 16.4, the parent's version. WebKit's expected results for the WPT haven't changed since that commit: srcdoc and data: pass, and blob: fails (iframe-loading-lazy-expected.txt). The manual test on Safari 26.4 matches.

Related issues

Fixes #30950
items.title: Add srcdoc, data: and blob: subfeatures to iframe loading

items.content_html:
Summary

Adds api.PerformanceObserver.observe.options_type_parameter. The method shipped with entryTypes only, and observe({ type: "..." }) came later, so the current data (Safari 11, Chrome 52, Firefox 57) overstates support for code that uses type.

I named it options_type_parameter instead of type_parameter, following the guideline for properties of parameter objects (same as options_capture_parameter on addEventListener()).

Test results and supporting details

Versions follow what @caugner found in #24584, and I checked each one against the source:

  • Chrome 74: "[PerformanceObserver] Ship |type| in PerformanceObserverInit" (e80ce141047415c1412c5c300f5ff206e45aa8b7), first in 74.0.3690.0 per chromiumdash.
  • Firefox 68: bug 1539006, target milestone mozilla68.
  • Safari 14: WebKit d37ab8ceef1841fad029605443a7177f805299fd (bug 209216), WebKit 610.1.24. Safari 13.1 is 609.1.20 and Safari 14 is 610.1.28.
  • Node.js 16.0.0: lib/perf_hooks.js in v15.14.0 only reads entryTypes; lib/internal/perf/observe.js in v16.0.0 reads type (nodejs/node#37136).
  • Deno 2.7: the first PerformanceObserver in ext/web/15_performance.js (denoland/deno#31875) already handles type, so same as the parent.
  • Bun 1.0.22: src/bun.js/bindings/webcore/PerformanceObserver.cpp at bun-v1.0.22 already handles init.type, so same as the parent.

observe({ type: "mark" }) delivers entries in Node 22 and Bun 1.3.11. npm run lint on the file passes and lint:fix makes no changes.

Related issues

Fixes #24584
items.title: Add `options.type` parameter to PerformanceObserver.observe()

items.content_html:
Summary

The Filter Effects spec says kernelUnitLength is deprecated on <feConvolveMatrix> and <feDiffuseLighting>, so this sets deprecated: true on those two attribute entries.

Test results and supporting details

Both attribute definitions in the current Filter Effects draft end with this note:

This attribute is deprecated and will be removed. It does not provide a reliable way to create platform independent results. Future versions of this specification will cover this use case.

See https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#element-attrdef-feconvolvematrix-kernelunitlength and the feDiffuseLighting definition right below it in the same spec.

I left svg.elements.feSpecularLighting.kernelUnitLength as it is, since its definition doesn't have that note. If you'd rather keep all three consistent, I'm happy to add it here.

Lint passes locally.

Related issues

Fixes #28178
items.title: Mark kernelUnitLength on feConvolveMatrix and feDiffuseLighting as deprecated
